extracted.intended_audience: public relations and communications professionals, marketers and writers preparing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing effective news/press releases that attract media pickup and reader engagement; covers structure, style (AP), length, SEO, multimedia, and distribution considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and informativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: A good press release is concise, informative and captures attention right from the start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the message clear and focused; avoid unnecessary words and jargon. Aim to present essential details so the release is easy to understand and promote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release structure (components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a standard layout: Headline, Dateline, Lead paragraph, Body content, Quote, Provide data, Call to action, Boilerplate, Media contact information, Images/video or other multimedia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All press releases tend to follow this layout, but effectiveness requires going beyond the template. Use each component for its purpose (e.g., lead = five Ws; boilerplate = org description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline — capture attention and show relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft a headline that answers 'Why should I care?' and prompts the audience to continue reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headline concise (guidance includes 'no more than 100 characters' and elsewhere 'aiming for 70 characters or less if possible'). Use strong action verbs, be specific, intriguing and informative. Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns (AP style). Include keywords and numbers/data where appropriate. Avoid ambiguous words, vague phrasing, jargon; write in active voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline format
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the city and date showing where and when the press release was issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the first paragraph with the city in ALL CAPS, followed by the state abbreviation and the date. Well-known cities may omit the state abbreviation (example: 'NEW YORK, May 6, 2024').

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph — the five Ws
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary of the essential details in the first paragraph using the five Ws: who, what, when, where and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with the most crucial information so journalists/readers immediately understand the news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body content — supporting details and quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand on the lead paragraph with supporting details and quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep paragraphs short, with one idea per paragraph. Follow the lead with quotes and additional context to build the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from a relevant stakeholder or expert to add credibility and a human touch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce quotes with the speaker’s full name and title on first reference (AP style). Use double quotation marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data / support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Back up any claims with relevant statistics, survey results, historical context or industry trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using data builds credibility and increases chances of pickup. Support messages with your own research or reputable external sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to action (CTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear call to action to encourage readers to take the next step (e.g., link to a microsite or landing page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align the CTA with the press release's goal — direct readers to the website, registration, contact, or further resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief description of the organization issuing the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight the organization's mission and expertise in a concise paragraph at the end of the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details for media inquiries, including names, emails and phone numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for journalists to follow up; include full contact details for a media representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of images, video, and multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding visual elements can increase engagement with your press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include high-quality images or video when relevant; multimedia can boost interest and shareability, especially for online distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand who your readers are (industry professionals, potential customers, broader audience) and tailor language and message accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider what aspects of the news will resonate and how the audience prefers to consume information; tailor tone, detail level and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concise (word count guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for a press release word count of 300 to 500 words to keep your message clear and focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter releases (~300 words) suit minor updates, time-sensitive news and teasers. Longer releases are appropriate for complex topics, research/reports, or major announcements requiring extra context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay relevant — explain why it matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell your audience why they should care; connect the story to current trends, industry developments or broader social issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A timely, relevant press release is more likely to be picked up by media outlets and engage readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a story / humanize the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the release like a mini-story with a clear beginning, middle and end that weaves a compelling narrative and invites curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quotes from someone directly affected by the story to make it more personal and relatable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate SEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply SEO best practices — incorporate relevant keywords, optimize headlines and descriptions and utilize backlinks to improve visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimizing for search engines helps press releases reach a broader audience and appear higher on SERPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide credibility through sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Support messages with statistics, research or industry reports to add authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite reputable sources (internal or external) to build trust; data-backed claims increase likelihood of media pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and refine (editing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit thoroughly for grammar, style and flow. Proofread to catch typos and awkward phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-read to ensure each word serves a purpose and that the key message is conveyed before promoting the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP Style guidelines for press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow Associated Press (AP) Style — the widely used standard for journalism and press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key AP rules provided: capitalize only the first word and proper nouns in headlines; dateline format (city in caps, state abbrev., date); spell out numbers one through nine and use numerals for 10+; use numerals for ages and percentages; date abbreviation rules (months when used with a date); use double quotation marks and introduce quotes with full name/title on first reference; capitalize job titles only before a name, lowercase after; spell out acronyms on first use with abbreviation in parentheses; use one space after a period; do not use the Oxford comma; begin with the five Ws and follow with quotes/supporting info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust length by announcement type
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose release length based on the type of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shorter releases for minor updates, time-sensitive items or teasers; use longer formats for complex topics, research reports or major announcements requiring background and technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review successful examples in your industry and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Study successful press releases within the same industry and those designed for the same purpose (product launch, event, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following similar, proven examples increases the chances your release will be noticed; adapt tone and structure to what performs in your sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and promotion considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond writing, choose the right distribution partner and promotional strategy to ensure media visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective distribution networks and reporting tools can extend reach (PR Newswire advertises distribution to 170+ countries and analytics to measure impact). Align distribution choices with target outlets and audience.
